policy: Every valid track must receive at least a canonical main genre.
Use a parent fallback plus review flags when a subtype is not defensible.
Artist-profile evidence is allowed; broad/conflicting labels require documented judgment.
Propose precise new taxonomy nodes, but merge synonyms as aliases.

tracks.title: EMBRACE THE NIGHT
tracks.rationale: The exact release is tagged Trance at 155 BPM, while Cleopard2000 describes a modern Trance/Hard Trance/Eurodance revival; Neo Trance is the best canonical fit.

tracks.title: Bring It Back
tracks.rationale: Siimon tags the exact recording as Trance; its contemporary rave production is best represented by the existing Neo Trance leaf.

tracks.title: Thrill
tracks.rationale: Beatport classifies the exact 148 BPM recording as Trance (Main Floor), directly supporting the new canonical leaf.

tracks.title: Adagio for Strings
tracks.rationale: The exact 140 BPM release is Main Floor Trance and the composition is widely described as uplifting trance; Uplifting Trance captures the musical form more precisely.

tracks.title: I Don't Even Like You

tracks.title: Babydoll
tracks.rationale: The exact 155 BPM recording is categorized broadly as Dance/Pop. Its accelerated pop-vocal techno format fits Hypertechno, but the specific leaf is inferred and review-flagged.

tracks.title: Journey
tracks.rationale: Linds' profile centers contemporary trance-rave with hardgroove percussion. With no stronger exact-track genre source, Neo Trance is the best artist-level classification.

tracks.title: Self Aware

proposed_main_genres.name: Latin Rave
proposed_main_genres.rationale: A canonical parent for fast Latin club hybrids whose identity is not adequately represented by Trance, House, Techno or generic Hard Dance.

placements.bpm_justification: The affected Nasty Club recordings and the creator's definition occupy approximately 150–165 BPM.

proposed_subgenres.name: Nasty Club
proposed_subgenres.bpm_justification: Noro$t defines the style around 150–165 BPM.
proposed_subgenres.rationale: Creator-defined fusion of Latin rhythms, guaracha/reggaeton, trance, hard house and techno; distinct enough to avoid flattening the tracks into a broad rave bucket.

proposed_subgenres.name: Trance (Main Floor)
proposed_subgenres.bpm_justification: The affected recordings are predominantly 147–150 BPM and therefore belong in the hard master folder.
proposed_subgenres.rationale: Beatport's current Trance (Main Floor) category repeatedly identifies these exact recordings and is more precise than a generic Trance fallback.

proposed_subgenres.name: Uplifting Trance
proposed_subgenres.bpm_justification: The two selected melodic/vocal recordings are 140 BPM, inside the 132–145 BPM master range.
proposed_subgenres.rationale: A recognized melodic trance form with euphoric builds and releases that are too specific for the Trance parent alone.

proposed_subgenres.name: Eurotrance
proposed_subgenres.bpm_justification: The affected recording is 144 BPM, inside the fast-tech master range.
proposed_subgenres.rationale: A recognized European melodic/dance-oriented trance style; the exact release explicitly identifies its Eurotrance program.

proposed_subgenres.name: Neo Rave
proposed_subgenres.bpm_justification: The affected exact releases are approximately 150–155 BPM, with one source tempo discrepancy documented on its track.
proposed_subgenres.rationale: A current Hard Dance / Hardcore store category. It remains separate from Neo Trance because the canonical parent and musical emphasis differ.

proposed_subgenres.name: Hard Bounce
proposed_subgenres.bpm_justification: The selected artist contexts belong to the high-energy 145+ BPM hard-bounce circuit.
proposed_subgenres.rationale: A recognized contemporary hard-dance style used by the artists in this scene; it should not be collapsed into Hardstyle or Hard Trance.

proposed_subgenres.name: Hard Trance Pop
proposed_subgenres.bpm_justification: The affected exact recording is 150 BPM.
proposed_subgenres.rationale: The creator's own description for a pop-forward sound harder than hard house and softer than hard techno; it is precise without duplicating Hard Trance.

proposed_aliases.rationale: Common closed spelling used by labels for the same established Hard Trance style; it must normalize to one node rather than create a duplicate.
